questions.explanation: Q = C V = 5 × 12 = 60 microcoulomb.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Two identical metal spheres carry charges +6 microcoulomb and -2 microcoulomb. They are touched together and then separated. The charge on each is
questions.explanation: Total charge is conserved: +4 microcoulomb shared equally by identical spheres gives +2 microcoulomb each.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A 1 microcoulomb charge moves 2 m along the direction of a uniform electric field of 500 N/C. The work done by the field is

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: What is polarisation of a dielectric in an electric field?
questions.answer: When a dielectric is placed in an electric field, its molecules get a dipole moment (induced in non-polar molecules, aligned in polar ones). This gives a net surface charge that sets up a field opposing the applied field, which reduces the net field inside the dielectric.
keyPoints: Internal field opposes and reduces the applied field
questions.explanation: This is why inserting a dielectric increases capacitance.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A charged comb attracts small uncharged pieces of paper. Explain why.
questions.answer: The field of the comb polarises the paper: the nearer side acquires the opposite charge and the farther side the same charge. The field is stronger at the nearer side, so the attraction on the near charge exceeds the repulsion on the far charge and there is a net force towards the comb.
keyPoints: Paper is polarised by the comb
Opposite charge induced on near side
Non-uniform field gives a net attraction
questions.explanation: A neutral object can be attracted to a charged one because of induced charges.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Resistors of 4 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A wire of resistance 10 ohm is cut into two equal halves, which are then joined in parallel. The equivalent resistance is
questions.explanation: Each half has 5 ohm and two 5 ohm resistors in parallel give 2.5 ohm.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A cell of emf 6 V has an internal resistance of 0.5 ohm. The current when its terminals are short-circuited is

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle enter the same uniform magnetic field perpendicularly with the same speed. The ratio of the radius of the alpha particle's path to that of the proton is
questions.explanation: r = m v/(q B); the alpha particle has four times the mass and twice the charge, so its radius is 4/2 = 2 times larger.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Distinguish between the emf and the terminal potential difference of a cell.
questions.answer: The emf is the potential difference between the terminals of a cell when no current is drawn (open circuit). The terminal potential difference V is measured when current I flows, and is less than the emf by the drop across the internal resistance, V = E - Ir.
keyPoints: emf is the open-circuit potential difference
Terminal pd is measured with current flowing
questions.explanation: During charging the terminal voltage is greater than the emf.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Why does placing a soft iron core inside a solenoid make its magnetic field much stronger?
questions.answer: Soft iron has a high relative permeability. The core becomes magnetised by the field of the solenoid and its magnetisation adds to the applied field, increasing the total field many times.
keyPoints: Core gets magnetised in the field
Its field adds to that of the current
questions.explanation: B = mu_0 mu_r n I with mu_r large for soft iron.

questions.q: The capacitive reactance of a 100 microfarad capacitor at 50 Hz is about
A series circuit has a resistance of 30 ohm and an inductive reactance of 40 ohm. Its impedance is
A 100 V (rms) AC source is connected to a series circuit with R = 30 ohm and X_L = 40 ohm. The average power consumed is
A DC motor draws a very large current at the instant it is switched on mainly because
options: the supply voltage is highest at that moment
the back emf is zero when the armature is at rest
the coil resistance is lowest then
the magnetic field is strongest then
questions.explanation: Back emf is proportional to speed; at rest it is zero, so the current is limited only by the small coil resistance.

questions.q: What are eddy currents? State one useful application.
questions.answer: Eddy currents are circulating currents induced in a bulk piece of conductor when the magnetic flux through it changes. They are used in induction furnaces to melt metals and in electromagnetic braking of trains.
keyPoints: Induced circulating currents in solid conductors
Applications such as induction furnace or magnetic braking
questions.explanation: They also cause unwanted heating in transformer cores.

questions.q: Why is electric power transmitted over long distances at very high voltage?
questions.answer: For a given power P = V I, a higher voltage means a smaller current. The power wasted as heat in the lines is I^2 R, so a smaller current reduces the loss greatly. Transformers step the voltage up for transmission and down for use.
keyPoints: P = VI, high V means low I
questions.explanation: Doubling the voltage cuts the line loss to one quarter for the same power.

questions.q: A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a thin lens
options: is deviated away from the axis
questions.explanation: Near the optical centre the two faces of a thin lens are parallel, so the ray emerges without any appreciable bending.

questions.q: A concave mirror forms a real image 40 cm from the mirror of an object placed 20 cm from it. The magnification is
questions.explanation: m = -v/u = -(-40)/(-20) = -2, so the image is inverted and twice the size.

questions.q: A short-sighted person has a far point at 50 cm. The power of the lens needed to see distant objects clearly is
questions.explanation: A concave lens of focal length -50 cm forms a virtual image of a distant object at the far point; P = 1/(-0.5) = -2 D.

questions.q: Which pattern has fringes of unequal width, the central one being twice as wide as the others?
questions.explanation: In single-slit diffraction the central maximum is twice as wide as the secondary maxima, whereas Young's fringes are of equal width.

questions.q: What is the angle of minimum deviation of a prism?
questions.answer: It is the smallest angle by which a prism can deviate a ray of light. It occurs when the ray passes symmetrically through the prism, with the angle of incidence equal to the angle of emergence.
keyPoints: Smallest deviation produced by the prism
Angle of incidence equals angle of emergence
Ray inside the prism is parallel to the base
questions.explanation: The refractive index is n = sin((A + D)/2)/sin(A/2).

questions.q: Why does a cut diamond sparkle so much?
questions.answer: Diamond has a very high refractive index (about 2.4), so its critical angle is small, about 24 degrees. Light entering the stone undergoes total internal reflection several times at the cut faces before emerging, which makes it flash brightly.
keyPoints: Repeated total internal reflection inside the stone
questions.explanation: Sin C = 1/n, so a high n gives a small critical angle.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: A 1 kg ball moves at 1 m/s. Taking h = 6.63 × 10^-34 J s, its de Broglie wavelength is about
questions.explanation: lambda = h/(m v) = 6.63 × 10^-34 m, far too small to observe, which is why everyday objects show no wave behaviour.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: The number of neutrons in the nucleus of uranium-235 (atomic number 92) is
questions.explanation: Neutrons = A - Z = 235 - 92 = 143.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: A graph of stopping potential against frequency of incident light for a photoelectric surface is a straight line. Its slope is
questions.explanation: From e V_0 = h f - phi, V_0 = (h/e) f - phi/e, so the slope is h/e.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: In Bohr's model the speed of an electron in the n = 2 orbit compared with that in the n = 1 orbit is
questions.explanation: The orbital speed is proportional to 1/n, so it halves when n changes from 1 to 2.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: State two observations of Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment and the conclusion drawn from them.
questions.answer: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil, and a very small number were deflected through large angles, a few even turning back. This showed that most of the atom is empty space and that its positive charge and mass are concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus.
keyPoints: A few deflected through large angles
Atom has a small dense positive nucleus
questions.explanation: The result disproved the plum-pudding model.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Why do heavy stable nuclei contain more neutrons than protons?
questions.answer: Protons repel one another by the electrostatic force, which grows as the number of protons rises. Extra neutrons add to the attractive short-range nuclear force without adding repulsion, and so help to hold a large nucleus together.
keyPoints: Proton-proton Coulomb repulsion increases with Z
questions.explanation: That is why the stability line bends above N = Z for heavy nuclei.

questions.q: A solution contains 1 mol of glucose and 9 mol of water. The mole fraction of glucose is
The SI unit of the cell constant (l/A) of a conductivity cell is
questions.explanation: Length divided by area has the unit m/m^2 = m^-1.

questions.q: For water Kb = 0.52 K kg/mol. The elevation in boiling point of a 0.2 molal solution of a non-volatile non-electrolyte is
When a lead storage battery discharges, the density of the sulphuric acid electrolyte
questions.explanation: Sulphuric acid is consumed to form lead sulphate at both electrodes, so the electrolyte becomes less dense.

questions.q: Distinguish between a primary cell and a secondary cell with one example of each.
questions.answer: A primary cell, such as a dry cell, produces current by an irreversible chemical reaction and cannot be recharged. A secondary cell, such as the lead storage battery, undergoes a reversible reaction and can be recharged by passing current in the opposite direction.
keyPoints: Primary: not rechargeable, e.g. dry cell
Secondary: rechargeable, e.g. lead storage battery
questions.explanation: A fuel cell converts the energy of fuel directly into electricity as long as fuel is supplied.

questions.q: Why does a 0.1 molal NaCl solution show nearly twice the depression of freezing point of a 0.1 molal glucose solution?
questions.answer: Freezing-point depression depends on the number of solute particles. Glucose does not dissociate, but NaCl dissociates into Na+ and Cl-, giving about twice as many particles, so the van't Hoff factor is close to 2 and the depression is nearly doubled.
keyPoints: Colligative property depends on number of particles
questions.explanation: The observed factor is slightly below 2 because of ion pairing in real solutions.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The unit of the rate constant for a second-order reaction is
questions.explanation: Rate = k[A]^2, so k = (mol L^-1 s^-1)/(mol L^-1)^2 = L mol^-1 s^-1.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: When acidified orange potassium dichromate oxidises an alcohol, the solution turns
questions.explanation: Dichromate (Cr in +6, orange) is reduced to green Cr3+.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: In a reaction the rate doubles when [A] is doubled and does not change when [B] is doubled. The rate law is
questions.explanation: The rate is proportional to [A] to the first power and independent of [B].

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: For a zero-order reaction the initial concentration of the reactant is doubled. The half-life
questions.explanation: For zero order t_half = [A]0/(2k), which is proportional to the initial concentration.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: State any three characteristic properties of transition metals.
questions.answer: Transition metals show variable oxidation states, form coloured compounds and complexes, are often paramagnetic, have high melting points and densities, and act as good catalysts.
keyPoints: Catalytic activity, paramagnetism, high melting points
questions.explanation: These properties come from partly filled d orbitals.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Scandium shows only the +3 oxidation state and zinc only +2, whereas manganese shows many. Explain.
questions.answer: Scandium loses its two 4s electrons and the one 3d electron to reach the stable noble-gas configuration of Sc3+. Zinc loses only its two 4s electrons because the 3d10 subshell is stable. Manganese has five 3d and two 4s electrons of similar energy, so many different numbers can be lost.
keyPoints: Mn has many d electrons available for bonding
questions.explanation: The maximum oxidation state rises to +7 at manganese.

questions.q: A bidentate ligand binds to the central metal through
questions.explanation: Denticity is the number of donor atoms by which a ligand binds.

questions.q: The oxidation state of nickel in K2[Ni(CN)4] is
questions.explanation: Two K+ give +2, so the complex ion is 2-; four CN- give -4, so nickel is +2.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3 is
questions.explanation: Six aqua ligands and chromium in the +3 state with three chloride counter ions.

questions.q: [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3 and [Cr(H2O)5Cl]Cl2.H2O are examples of which type of isomerism?
questions.explanation: The isomers differ in the number of water molecules inside and outside the coordination sphere.

questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment of the high-spin complex [Fe(H2O)6]2+ (four unpaired electrons) is about
questions.explanation: mu = root(4 × 6) = root 24, which is about 4.90 BM.

questions.q: Write the IUPAC name of [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2.
questions.answer: Pentaamminechloridocobalt(III) chloride. Five ammine ligands, one chlorido ligand, cobalt in the +3 state, and two chloride counter ions.
keyPoints: Ligands named alphabetically: ammine then chlorido
questions.explanation: The oxidation state is found from the total charge of +2 on the cation.

questions.q: How is EDTA used in the estimation of hardness of water?
questions.answer: EDTA forms very stable, soluble complexes with Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions. The hard water is titrated with a standard EDTA solution using an indicator, and the volume used gives the total concentration of these ions.
keyPoints: EDTA is a hexadentate chelating ligand
Forms stable complexes with Ca2+ and Mg2+
questions.explanation: The indicator changes colour when all the metal ions have been complexed.

questions.q: Which of the following is an aryl halide?
questions.explanation: In an aryl halide the halogen is bonded directly to an sp2 carbon of an aromatic ring.

questions.q: Which reagent oxidises a primary alcohol to an aldehyde without further oxidation to the acid?
questions.explanation: PCC is a mild oxidising agent that stops at the aldehyde stage.

questions.q: Nitration of phenol with dilute nitric acid at low temperature gives
options: a mixture of o- and p-nitrophenol
questions.explanation: The -OH group directs the incoming group to the ortho and para positions.

questions.q: Which isomer of nitrophenol is steam volatile?
questions.explanation: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, so it is less associated and volatile, whereas p-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.q: Methylmagnesium bromide reacts with methanal, and the product is hydrolysed. The final product is
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents add to methanal to give primary alcohols with one more carbon, here CH3CH2OH.

questions.q: Distinguish between SN1 and SN2 reactions in terms of kinetics.
questions.answer: SN1 is a two-step reaction through a carbocation and its rate depends only on the haloalkane concentration, so it is first order. SN2 occurs in one step with the nucleophile attacking from the back, so its rate depends on both haloalkane and nucleophile and it is second order.
keyPoints: Rate of SN2 depends on nucleophile concentration
questions.explanation: Tertiary halides favour SN1 and primary halides favour SN2.

questions.q: Why does the boiling point of haloalkanes increase in the order RCl < RBr < RI for the same alkyl group?
questions.answer: The size and molar mass of the halogen increase from Cl to I, so the molecule has a larger surface area and more polarisable electrons. The van der Waals forces between molecules become stronger, and more energy is needed to separate them.
keyPoints: Larger halogen means greater molar mass and surface area
questions.explanation: For isomeric haloalkanes branching lowers the boiling point.

questions.q: Methanoic acid (formic acid) is naturally present in
questions.explanation: The name comes from the Latin word for ant; it is injected in ant stings.

questions.q: Ethanal on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride gives
questions.explanation: Aldehydes are reduced to primary alcohols.

questions.q: Aniline treated with nitrous acid (NaNO2 and HCl) at 0 to 5 degrees C gives
questions.explanation: Primary aromatic amines form diazonium salts at low temperature.

questions.q: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives an equimolar mixture of
questions.explanation: The mixture, called invert sugar, is laevorotatory because fructose is strongly laevorotatory.

questions.q: The alpha and beta forms of D-glucose are called anomers because they differ in configuration at
questions.explanation: They differ only in the orientation of the -OH group at the anomeric carbon C1 formed in ring closure.

questions.q: Distinguish between fibrous and globular proteins with an example of each.
questions.answer: Fibrous proteins have long thread-like polypeptide chains held side by side, are insoluble in water and serve structural roles, for example keratin and myosin. Globular proteins fold into a spherical shape, are soluble in water and perform functions such as catalysis, for example enzymes and insulin.
keyPoints: Globular: spherical, water soluble, e.g. insulin
questions.explanation: The shape is decided by the secondary and tertiary structure.

questions.q: Why are aliphatic amines stronger bases than ammonia in the gas phase?
questions.answer: Alkyl groups release electrons by the +I effect, which increases the electron density on nitrogen. The lone pair is then more available to accept a proton, and the ammonium ion formed is stabilised by the alkyl groups, so alkylamines are stronger bases than ammonia.
questions.explanation: In water, solvation and steric effects change the order among primary, secondary and tertiary amines.

questions.q: The release of the ovum from the Graafian follicle is called
questions.explanation: Ovulation occurs around the middle of the menstrual cycle.

questions.q: Yeast reproduces asexually mainly by
questions.explanation: A small bud grows out of the parent cell and separates to form a new yeast cell.

questions.q: Gametes in humans are formed by
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, producing haploid gametes.

questions.q: How many pollen mother cells must undergo meiosis to produce 100 pollen grains?
questions.explanation: Each pollen mother cell gives four haploid pollen grains, so 100/4 = 25 are needed.

questions.q: In the human male, luteinising hormone acts on the
questions.explanation: LH stimulates the Leydig (interstitial) cells, whereas FSH acts on the Sertoli cells.

questions.q: What is parturition?
questions.answer: Parturition is the process of giving birth, in which the fully developed foetus is expelled from the uterus through the vagina at the end of pregnancy, brought about by powerful uterine contractions.
keyPoints: Controlled by hormones such as oxytocin
questions.explanation: In humans pregnancy lasts about nine months.

questions.q: What is the role of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in early pregnancy?
questions.answer: hCG is secreted by the developing placental tissue. It maintains the corpus luteum so that it keeps secreting progesterone, which preserves the endometrium and prevents menstruation. It is also the basis of pregnancy tests.
questions.explanation: Later the placenta itself secretes enough progesterone.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Which type of RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during translation?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA brings specific amino acids and reads the codon through its anticodon.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: How many different types of gametes can an individual of genotype AaBb produce, assuming independent assortment?
questions.explanation: AB, Ab, aB and ab are formed in equal numbers.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Mendel's law of independent assortment holds good for genes that are
options: very close on the same chromosome
questions.explanation: Genes on different chromosomes assort independently during meiosis; closely linked genes tend to be inherited together.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Morgan's work on Drosophila showed that genes located close together on the same chromosome
options: show linkage and a low frequency of recombination
are always on the X chromosome
questions.explanation: Linked genes are inherited together more often than expected, and the closer they are the lower the recombination frequency.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Phenylketonuria is an autosomal recessive disorder. Two phenotypically normal carrier parents have a child. The probability that the child is affected is
questions.explanation: Aa × Aa gives 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa, so one in four is affected.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: What are mutations? Name two types.
questions.answer: Mutations are sudden heritable changes in the DNA of an organism. They include point mutations, which change a single base pair (such as in sickle-cell anaemia), and chromosomal mutations such as deletion, duplication or changes in chromosome number.
questions.explanation: Mutations are a source of variation for evolution.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: What is adaptive radiation? Give one example.
questions.answer: Adaptive radiation is the evolution of many different forms from a common ancestor in one geographical area, each adapted to a different habitat or way of life. Darwin's finches in the Galapagos Islands, with differently shaped beaks, are an example.
keyPoints: Example Darwin's finches or Australian marsupials
questions.explanation: It is a process of divergent evolution.

questions.q: The restriction enzyme EcoRI is obtained from
questions.explanation: The name EcoRI comes from the genus Escherichia, the species coli and the strain RY13.

questions.q: A plasmid vector such as pBR322 contains genes for
options: antibiotic resistance, which act as selectable markers
questions.explanation: Antibiotic-resistance genes allow selection of the bacteria that have taken up the plasmid.

questions.q: A high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of a water sample indicates
options: water rich in dissolved oxygen only
questions.explanation: BOD is the oxygen used by microbes to break down organic matter, so a high value means heavy organic pollution.

questions.q: Water hyacinth is a serious problem in Indian water bodies because it
options: grows very rapidly and depletes oxygen, harming aquatic life
adds extra oxygen to the water
questions.explanation: It is an invasive alien species that forms dense mats, blocking light and lowering dissolved oxygen.

questions.q: In the gene gun (biolistics) method of gene transfer into plant cells, the DNA is
options: coated on microscopic gold or tungsten particles fired into the cells
injected into the nucleus with a fine needle
added with calcium ions to bacteria
questions.explanation: High-velocity microparticles coated with DNA are shot through the cell wall into plant cells.

questions.q: Name two methods of ex situ conservation.
questions.answer: Examples are zoos and botanical gardens, seed banks, gene banks and cryopreservation of gametes at very low temperature in liquid nitrogen.
questions.explanation: These methods safeguard endangered species outside their natural habitats.

questions.q: Explain the greenhouse effect and name one consequence of its enhancement.
questions.answer: Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorb the infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and re-radiate part of it back, keeping the planet warm. Increased emissions from human activity strengthen this effect and cause global warming, leading to melting of ice and rising sea level.
keyPoints: Enhancement causes global warming and sea-level rise
questions.explanation: Without the natural greenhouse effect the Earth would be much colder.
